ptr.note: A live pool (never NULL), shared: C locks pool->mutex around the free list and the allocator call, and bumps the atomic 32-bit pool refcount (relaxed, unchecked) per buffer handed out; each such count is backed by >= 112 bytes of live C heap (entry + AVBufferRef), so wrapping it takes ~480 GB of leaked buffers. Rust: BufferPoolRef::get / get_with_opaque on the shared handle (the pool is Sync).

A new sole, writable reference (flags 0, count 1): a recycled entry's pool->size bytes (contents left by their previous user) or a fresh allocator buffer (av_buffer_alloc: uninitialised; custom allocators: their reference as returned, its AVBuffer's flags_internal included, so a first buffer from an allocator returning reallocatable buffers is itself BUFFER_FLAG_REALLOCATABLE; recycled entries are rebuilt with flags 0 and BUFFER_FLAG_NO_FREE). Its release returns the entry to the pool (pool_release_buffer) and drops the pool count, freeing the pool after av_buffer_pool_uninit and the last return. NULL on allocator or entry/AVBufferRef allocation failure. Rust: UninitBuffer (released by av_buffer_unref), built directly: the bytes are the allocator buffer's, which no release reads as initialised (av_buffer_alloc blocks or an allocator's own UninitBuffer).
